task_title: Create the package, tooling, and docs scaffold around the planned feature surface

artifacts.description: Packaging and development tooling configuration for editable installs, tests, linting, typing, and docs.
Typed Phase 1 feature matrix and namespace plan anchored to the local Tidy3D-inspired checklist.
CLI entrypoint exposing the packaged feature matrix for smoke testing and inspection.
Top-level package exports for versioning and planning metadata.
Reserved `src`-layout package namespaces for API, IR, compiler, runtime, kernels, diagnostics, and feature families.
MkDocs configuration for the new documentation scaffold.
Documentation scaffold covering overview, architecture, feature matrix, and development entrypoints.
Import, planning, and CLI smoke tests validating the scaffold.
Repository README expanded to describe package layout, quick start, and development commands.
Condensed Phase 1 handoff notes recording scaffold decisions for later tasks.

follow_up_notes: Next logical work is `task-002`: populate `autofdtd.api` and `autofdtd.core` with the tagged immutable `Simulation`, `Scene`, and `Structure` models while preserving the reserved subsystem layout established here.
key_findings: The repository now has a buildable/editable package scaffold using `hatchling` in `pyproject.toml` with test, lint, type-check, and docs entrypoints.
Phase 1 feature-planning is encoded in `src/autofdtd/planning.py`, giving later tasks a local typed source for feature status and reserved namespace boundaries instead of relying only on markdown.

Subsystem namespaces are reserved up front for `api`, `core`, `geometry`, `materials`, `boundaries`, `sources`, `monitors`, `grid`, `modes`, `ir`, `compiler`, `runtime`, `kernels`, `diagnostics`, and `examples`.
A concrete install smoke target now exists via the `autofdtd-feature-matrix` CLI, which renders the packaged Phase 1 feature matrix in table or JSON form.
Validation passed for editable install, package imports, CLI tests, `pytest`, `ruff`, `mypy`, and `mkdocs build`.
message: Created a pip-installable `src`-layout `autofdtd` package scaffold with subsystem namespaces, development tooling, a code-backed Phase 1 feature matrix, tests, and MkDocs documentation aligned to the Phase 1 feature checklist and solver subsystem boundaries.
task_title: Create the package, tooling, and docs scaffold around the planned feature surface
Implement the tagged core Simulation, Scene, and Structure data model

artifacts.description: Frozen tagged container models and precedence/serialization helpers for `Structure`, `Scene`, and `Simulation`.
Public API re-exports for the foundational container models.
API namespace exports exposing the new container backbone.
Core namespace exports exposing the tagged container layer.
Container-model tests for names, precedence ordering, conductor priority defaults, and JSON serialization.
Architecture notes updated to describe the current container backbone and separation from future IR work.
Condensed handoff notes capturing the container-model decisions for later tasks.
Task board updated to mark `task-002` completed.
Recorded task output matching the Phase 1 result schema.

follow_up_notes: `task-003` should now define the separate execution IR contract and treat the current container payload helpers as an interim handoff format rather than the final IR schema.
key_findings: `src/autofdtd/core/containers.py` now provides frozen pydantic container models with explicit `type` tags, JSON-ready payload helpers, and minimal disk serialization entrypoints.

`Scene` preserves ordered structure semantics and exposes `structures_in_resolution_order()` so later scene compilation can apply structures by resolved priority and insertion order without re-deriving precedence rules.

`StructurePriorityMode.CONDUCTOR` is mapped early using medium type tags so implicit priority behavior can distinguish dielectric, lossy-metal, and PEC structures before concrete material classes land.

`Simulation` now carries the Phase 1 shell fields from the feature checklist, including domain size, run time, sources, monitors, boundary and grid references, symmetry, shutoff, courant, and subpixel references.

Focused tests now cover name normalization, duplicate-name rejection, ordered overlap behavior, conductor-priority defaults, and tagged JSON serialization, and the repo passes `pytest`, `ruff`, and `mypy`.
message: Implemented the first tagged immutable container backbone for `Simulation`, `Scene`, and `Structure`, including ordered structure precedence helpers, name validation, and JSON-ready serialization scaffolding for later IR work.
task_title: Implement the tagged core Simulation, Scene, and Structure data model
Define the tagged execution IR and serialization contract

artifacts.description: Versioned execution IR models, lowering helpers, bundle writer, and JSON-schema export helpers.
IR namespace exports for the new execution contract.
Coverage for simulation lowering, bundle serialization, and schema inspection.
Architecture notes describing the execution IR and packaging contract.
Updated distilled decisions and handoff notes for later validation and model-base tasks.

follow_up_notes: Verification passed with `pytest -q`, `ruff check .`, and `mypy src`. The next tasks can build normalization and shared model-base work on top of the new IR schema/version constants and `ComponentIR` envelope.
key_findings: Added `autofdtd.ir` models for `ComponentIR`, `StructureIR`, `SceneIR`, `SimulationIR`, `ArtifactIR`, `ExecutionManifestIR`, and `ExecutionPackageIR` under schema version `phase1.v1`.

Lowering from the public container layer is now explicit via `component_to_ir()`, `structure_to_ir()`, `scene_to_ir()`, and `simulation_to_ir()`, keeping the execution IR independent from the API module layout while preserving ordered structure semantics and resolved priorities.

Bundle packaging is directory-based: `manifest.json` records package format `autofdtd.execution-package.v1` and a hashed `simulation.json` entrypoint artifact, avoiding self-referential manifest hashing while remaining suitable for local or remote transport.

Validation now covers the IR schema version, package format, and component envelope basics, and the contract is backed by JSON-schema export plus tests for lowering, bundle writing, and schema inspection.
message: Implemented a versioned execution IR and bundle serialization contract for Phase 1, including public lowering helpers, manifest-based packaging, schema export, tests, and architecture/docs updates.

Implement core normalization and validation behavior

artifacts.description: Shared Phase 1 validation and normalization helpers for tagged component payloads and simulation-bound checks.
Integrated container-level validators for geometry, media, boundaries, normalize-index, and deferred-feature policies.
Added feature lookup helpers and extra tracked Phase 1 feature tags used by validation.
Validation coverage for normalization, shape constraints, unsupported features, domain bounds, and zero-dimension boundary coercion.
Architecture notes describing the new shared validation layer and its current responsibilities.
Distilled task handoff notes for later feature-family tasks to reuse the core validation path.
Structured task result artifact for this loop iteration.

follow_up_notes: Verification passed with `ruff check`, `pytest -q`, and `mypy src`. Geometry, material, boundary, source, monitor, and grid tasks should extend `autofdtd.core.validation` rather than duplicating checklist-driven policy checks in each family.
key_findings: Added `autofdtd.core.validation` as the shared normalization layer for tagged component payloads, covering name trimming, vector coercion, primitive geometry checks for `Box`/`Sphere`/`Cylinder`, structure-bound checks against the simulation domain, and zero-size-axis boundary coercion to `Periodic`.

`Simulation` now exposes explicit Phase 1 control-policy fields for `normalize_index`, `relax_courant`, `low_freq_smoothing`, and `lumped_elements`, with implemented validation for normalize-index and clear fail-fast errors for deferred or rejected core features.

Unsupported feature handling is now tied directly to the local feature matrix through lookup helpers in `autofdtd.planning`, so deferred and reject-clearly feature tags fail with explicit messages instead of being accepted silently or rejected as unknown extras.

Coverage now includes normalization, primitive shape errors, out-of-domain warnings and errors, zero-dimension absorbing-boundary coercion, normalize-index validation, and planning lookups, with docs and working memory updated to point later tasks at the shared validator path.
message: Implemented checklist-aware core normalization and validation for the Phase 1 container layer, including primitive-shape sanity checks, simulation-bound validation, explicit unsupported-feature errors, normalize-index handling, zero-dimension boundary coercion, and supporting tests/docs.

`Structure`, `Scene`, `Simulation`, and all IR models now inherit shared serialization and `copy_update()` behavior instead of duplicating helpers in subsystem-local base classes.
Exported the shared base types through `autofdtd.core`, `autofdtd.api`, and package root so later feature families can depend on one stable model surface.
Extended tests to cover generic tag lookup, immutable copy/update behavior, and shared helper usage across both API and IR layers.

message: Implemented a shared frozen model contract for tagging, copy-or-update, and JSON serialization, then moved the public container and IR layers onto it with passing tests.

artifacts.description: Typed public wrapper models for grouped, transformed, and clipped geometry composition.

`GeometryTransform` now supports rigid composition plus translation, rotation, reflection, and conservative transformed-bounds evaluation, which both scene queries and IR lowering reuse.
Geometry validation now explicitly permits the implemented clip subset while still treating the wider `ClipOperation` family as deferred and rejecting unsupported boolean ops with clear errors.
Execution IR now lowers composite geometry into typed `GeometryGroupIR`, `TransformedIR`, and `ClipOperationIR` payloads instead of falling back to the generic component envelope.
Representative docs and examples now cover composite geometry usage, and verification passed with `ruff check src tests` and `pytest -q`.

follow_up_notes: Verification run: `ruff check src tests` and `pytest -q tests/test_containers.py tests/test_ir.py`. Full-suite execution was not run.
key_findings: Added `GeometryArray` with Tidy3D-inspired `geometry + offsets + transforms` semantics, with Phase 1 validation that keeps transforms rigid and linear-only and reserves translation for offsets.

Made structure precedence explicit via `Scene.structure_precedence()` and `Scene.resolve_structure_stack_at_point()`, and mirrored that metadata into `StructureIR` with `source_index` and `precedence_rank`.

Lowered `GeometryArray` into ordinary grouped/transformed geometry during IR conversion instead of inventing a separate array execution primitive, keeping ordered materialization semantics consistent.
Updated docs and examples to cover repeated placement, and verified the behavior with targeted container/IR tests plus linting.
message: Implemented Phase 1 repeated-placement geometry and explicit structure precedence: `GeometryArray` is now part of the public API, overlap order is surfaced as concrete metadata, arrays lower into explicit grouped instances in IR, and docs/examples/tests cover the behavior.

`Simulation.resolved_grid()` and `core.validation` now enforce a strict top-level `GridSpec` contract, validate manual grid compatibility against simulation bounds, and reject planned-but-not-yet-implemented grid families like `AutoGrid` explicitly.

Public exports, examples, and docs were updated so the grid surface is part of the Tidy3D-inspired API rather than an opaque dict payload.
Verification passed with `python -m ruff check src tests` and `python -m pytest` (47 tests passed).

key_findings: `src/autofdtd/grid/specs.py` now includes `AutoGrid`, `GridRefinement`, and `LayerRefinementSpec`, and `GridSpec` can resolve wavelength-driven AutoGrid axes with axis-aligned layer refinement and a simple `max_scale` grading pass.

Validation and planning metadata were updated so `AutoGrid` and refinement specs are accepted, `GridSpec.wavelength` is required for AutoGrid axes, and `QuasiUniformGrid` remains an explicit deferred error.
Coverage was added for AutoGrid spacing, layer snapping/refinement behavior, container normalization, and IR lowering; `pytest tests/test_containers.py tests/test_grid.py tests/test_ir.py` passes.
message: Implemented a first Phase 1 AutoGrid and refinement planning surface with typed public models, concrete resolution behavior, IR lowering, docs, examples, and passing validation tests.

message: Implemented the Phase 1 subpixel policy surface with explicit `SubpixelSpec`, typed averaging and staircasing models, Tidy3D-style boolean coercion, and typed IR metadata for later geometry materialization.

`autofdtd.kernels.materials` now allocates explicit per-pole polarization state and provides `pole_residue_electric_update()` for staged dispersive electric updates.
Scene-level material sampling and coefficient attachment now cover dispersive media as well as isotropic and conductor cases.
Verification passed with `pytest -q` and `python -m compileall src`.
message: Implemented Phase 1 PoleResidue medium support with validated public and IR models, coefficient preparation, explicit auxiliary-state handling, staged dispersive electric updates, and representative tests/docs/examples.
